Messages.Author: ICL
Messages.Body:
Really, it's decks that don't let other people play the game. In terms of most egregious in that category by measure of consistency of causing one specific player to lose, off the top of my head, vamp steal deck.

Winnie deck won't let a prey play the game, rush will often remove a player's ability to play, Brainwash, First Tradition's whole point is to lock players out of the game, Sensory Deprivation, etc. But, Spirit Marionette, Mind Rape, even Temptation fall into some category of being easy enough to pull off with too high of a probability of removing one player's ability to meaningfully participate.

I certainly hate plenty of other decks. Imbued are just tedious, made even more so by the unnecessary whining that often occurs when they see play. Brinksmanship decks would be similar. Walls. And, various that don't come readily to mind.

@ Kiddo and Ashur. Both of your examples are valid examples. But I might call stuff that plays 4 bounces in 90 cards for "toolbox without bounce" as well, since it's essentially with it.

But Toolboxes without bounce includ but are not limited to: Gangrel, !gangrel, akunanse, nos, !nos, brujah, !brujah, etc etc. The lists goes on. Point being; I really hate facing crappy decks that don't have any place in a tournament enviorment. Typiclly thay end up blocking a few actions, rush once or twice (probably backwards) and then gives its prey to much room to build up. Leading to that players prey likey to win.

That's real frustration for me. Good player playing sleazy tried and true decks - that's what I really like (though sleazy but innovative decks is just as fine).

Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
The question is "what decktype do you hate". Not "which decktype do you find most annoying when it's played or built poorly".

I think it's pretty evident that decks that sit like lumps, gain pool and do nothing are annoying. That's not an archtype tho. The Girls... archtype does, contrary to popular believe by those who didn't extensively play it *not* only gain pool. Yes, you can build it like that and then you'd have a bad deck, similar to how you can pilot a totally retarded Beast rush deck with 70 red cards.

Don't confuse "I hate that deck" with "I hate it when people play stupid decks" or "I hate that awful player unless he's my predator/prey".

That said, I voted Imbued for the same reason I voted Direct Intervention - they disrupt the game.

Their mechanics are different, they don't interact well with actual vampire cards and you either can't do anything to them or you completely roll them over.
